title: LARGE CERAMIC LIDDED ELEPHANT ...
reason: Big, well-modelled decorative elephant jar of unidentified maker with base marks not shown; could be a named Italian or studio piece worth more, otherwise a decorative piece in the $80-150 range.
findings: Large cream-white crackle-glazed ceramic elephant jar with a lift-off lid topped by a baby elephant finial (amber-tinted eye). Crisp moulded relief: wheat-ear and leaf panelled caparison, beaded borders and pineapple or cone shaped tassels, detailed eye and ear. Unglazed buff foot rims and a buff, lightly glazed or unglazed interior (photo 3) suggest an earthenware or stoneware body. No maker's mark, signature or label seen in any photo; the base and the underside of the lid were not shown clearly, so the maker is unknown. Style looks mid to late 20th century decorative ware (possibly an Italian or Asian import); web searches found no match. The title size (H-47 L-49 cm) makes it a big decorative piece.
condition: Overall fine glaze crazing; worn unglazed foot rims; dark specks or staining inside the jar (photo 3); a wisp of fibre on the baby elephant's head (photo 1); no chips, cracks or repairs seen in the photos but the base is unseen; lid appears to fit.
rescore_note: Big, well-modelled cream crackle-glaze elephant jar with lid, but unmarked and unidentified (looks like a mid to late 20th century decorative import), with staining inside; no comparable found; my estimate $50 to 120.
